gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 6?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent high-resolution forecasts from the German Weather Service (DWD), ECMWF, and ICON models indicate a maximum temperature in Munich on September 6 near 24°C under mostly sunny skies and light northeasterly flow, driving the strong market preference for 24°C. This outlook sits slightly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 21.2°C, supported by stable high pressure and minimal cloud cover that limits daytime heating variability. Ensemble spreads remain narrow, with only modest differences across runs keeping probabilities concentrated on 24–25°C. Updated model guidance and official DWD briefings tomorrow morning represent the final data points before market resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Met Office forecasts project a maximum of 26°C for London on September 6 under partly cloudy skies with light southerly winds, supporting surface heating without significant cloud cover or precipitation to suppress temperatures. This aligns closely with model consensus and places the day well above the 1991–2020 average high of 21°C. Hourly guidance shows peaks near 25–26°C in the afternoon, with limited upside potential from localized urban heat effects or brief clearer spells that could nudge readings to 27°C at some sites. Downside risks remain modest given stable high pressure and minimal frontal activity, keeping the distribution of implied probabilities concentrated on 26°C and 27°C as the most likely resolution outcomes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple sources, including NWS-aligned models, project a sunny Monday in New York City with northwest winds of 5–10 mph supporting a daily high near 78–81 °F, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting on those bins. This outlook reflects seasonal norms for early September, when average highs hover around 79 °F, and follows a cooler, partly showery weekend that has allowed high pressure to build. Model consensus remains tight with minimal spread, though minor adjustments could arise from the final National Weather Service update or localized urban heat effects before observations close. Traders appear to view the 80–81 °F outcome as the most probable given current atmospheric conditions and the absence of any incoming fronts.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent heavy rainfall and thick cloud cover from an active frontal system are suppressing daytime warming in Tokyo today, keeping the maximum temperature tightly clustered around 23°C.** Multiple official and model forecasts, including those aligned with Japan Meteorological Agency guidance, show daytime highs of 23–24°C under overcast skies, northerly to northeasterly winds, and near-100% precipitation probability with locally heavy rain. These conditions limit solar heating and advect cooler maritime air, preventing the typical early-September afternoon climb toward 26–28°C.

Trader consensus reflected in the 75% implied probability for 23°C (with 24°C at 18%) tracks this forecast consensus closely. Higher outcomes (25°C+) carry low odds because any break in the rain or unexpected clearing would still face limited insolation and ongoing moisture. Lower readings remain improbable given the current thermal profile and observed temperatures already in the low-20s°C range. Updated model runs and real-time observations from monitoring agencies will determine final resolution, but the dominant rain event continues to anchor probabilities near the current leading outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from National Weather Service and private models places the September 6 high for New York City (Central Park or airport sites) in the mid-70s, aligning closely with the market’s leading bins of 74-75°F (47.5%) and 76-77°F (29%).** 

Cooler northeasterly flow has replaced the warmer air mass that produced highs near 81–86°F on September 5, limiting daytime heating. Partly to mostly cloudy skies and a 20–50% chance of light showers or drizzle further reduce solar insolation, keeping maximum temperatures below the late-summer climatological average of ~79.5°F. Model guidance shows little spread, with most runs converging on 74–76°F; the modest probability mass on 72–73°F (19%) reflects residual uncertainty over shower timing and cloud thickness, while tails below 70°F or above 78°F remain near 1% or less given current steering patterns and boundary-layer moisture. 

Upcoming hourly observations and any late-morning model updates will provide the final resolution data for this single-day temperature market.

These conditions stem from a moist, unstable airmass with southwesterly flow and high humidity, which reduces solar insolation and promotes evaporative cooling. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread, with most runs clustering in the 25–30°C range and only modest potential for brief clearing to push readings higher. Historical September averages near 29°C provide context, yet the active precipitation pattern this week deviates from drier climatology. Updated model runs and official JMA briefings over the next 48 hours will clarify whether any late-day breaks allow temperatures to reach the upper end of the distribution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from National Weather Service and private models places the September 6 high for New York City (Central Park or airport sites) in the mid-70s, aligning closely with the market’s leading bins of 74-75°F (47.5%) and 76-77°F (29%).** 

Cooler northeasterly flow has replaced the warmer air mass that produced highs near 81–86°F on September 5, limiting daytime heating. Partly to mostly cloudy skies and a 20–50% chance of light showers or drizzle further reduce solar insolation, keeping maximum temperatures below the late-summer climatological average of ~79.5°F. Model guidance shows little spread, with most runs converging on 74–76°F; the modest probability mass on 72–73°F (19%) reflects residual uncertainty over shower timing and cloud thickness, while tails below 70°F or above 78°F remain near 1% or less given current steering patterns and boundary-layer moisture. 

Upcoming hourly observations and any late-morning model updates will provide the final resolution data for this single-day temperature market.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Clear skies, high pressure, and light northeasterly winds are driving Munich’s temperature toward a peak near 24°C today (September 6, 2026), aligning with the market’s strong 68.5% implied probability on that outcome.** 

Forecast models (including GFS-based runs) show sunny conditions with minimal cloud cover through the afternoon, allowing strong solar insolation under a stable anticyclone (surface pressure ~1028 hPa). Light winds (generally 4–10 km/h) limit mixing and evaporative cooling, while low humidity and negligible precipitation chance (0–2%) support efficient daytime heating. Observed morning temperatures starting in the low-to-mid teens °C have climbed steadily, consistent with hourly trends reaching the low 20s by midday and peaking in the early-to-mid afternoon.

This setup places the daily maximum above the 1991–2020 September average high of ~21°C but well below historical extremes (record 29°C). Consensus across sources clusters tightly around 23–25°C, with 24°C as the modal expectation; the modest 25% probability on 25°C reflects the realistic upper end of model spread under continued clear conditions, while lower outcomes (23°C or below) carry limited weight given current observations and the absence of cooling factors such as increased cloudiness or stronger winds. Updated model runs and real-time station data through the afternoon will be the key near-term drivers for any shifts in trader positioning.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from the German Weather Service (DWD) and Met Office indicate a daytime high near 27°C for Munich on September 7, driven by southwesterly flow, mostly clear to partly cloudy skies, and light winds under a stable high-pressure pattern. This exceeds the 1991–2020 average high of 21°C while remaining well below the September 7 record of 29.6°C. Ensemble forecasts show a tight range centered on 26–28°C with limited model spread, supporting the market's leading outcomes at 27°C (40%), 26°C (24%), and 28°C (18.5%). Updated runs overnight and morning observations will refine peak timing and any cloud-cover impacts ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from ECMWF, GFS, and ICON runs positions 27°C as the leading outcome for Munich’s September 7 maximum, with ensemble spreads favoring 26–28°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies, light westerly to southwesterly flow, and only isolated shower chances below 15%. This reflects a stable high-pressure ridge suppressing stronger warming while allowing modest diurnal rise above the 21°C September climatological average. Low precipitation and dew points in the mid-teens support efficient daytime heating without significant cloud cover or moisture constraints. Traders appear to weight the latest deterministic guidance most heavily, with 27°C holding the highest implied probability at 41% ahead of tomorrow’s official DWD observations that will resolve the market.

gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 8?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models, including outputs from the German Weather Service (DWD) and international ensembles, indicate a southerly flow advecting warmer air masses into southern Bavaria, supporting daytime maxima of 29–31 °C in Munich on September 8. This setup, combined with partly cloudy skies and light southwesterly winds, favors strong daytime heating under late-summer insolation, pushing temperatures well above the 20.9 °C climatological average while remaining within historical extremes for the date. Forecast consensus across global and regional models shows limited spread on peak values, though minor timing differences in cloud cover or frontal approach could shift the exact maximum by 1–2 °C. Trader positioning around 31 °C reflects this tight range of guidance, with lower probabilities assigned to cooler or much hotter outliers pending the next model updates.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from ECMWF, GFS, and ICON runs positions 27°C as the leading outcome for Munich’s September 7 maximum, with ensemble spreads favoring 26–28°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies, light westerly to southwesterly flow, and only isolated shower chances below 15%. This reflects a stable high-pressure ridge suppressing stronger warming while allowing modest diurnal rise above the 21°C September climatological average. Low precipitation and dew points in the mid-teens support efficient daytime heating without significant cloud cover or moisture constraints. Traders appear to weight the latest deterministic guidance most heavily, with 27°C holding the highest implied probability at 41% ahead of tomorrow’s official DWD observations that will resolve the market.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models including ECMWF and ICON indicate a peak daily maximum near 30–31°C in Munich on September 8, driven by southwesterly flow advecting warmer air masses ahead of an approaching frontal system, combined with strong daytime insolation under partly cloudy skies. This setup supports surface heating above the long-term average high of about 21°C, though model spread and potential for increased cloud cover or earlier showers introduce uncertainty around exact maxima. Traders appear to weigh these conditions against historical records near 29.6°C, with updated runs and official DWD guidance expected to refine probabilities before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent heavy rainfall and a stationary front off Japan's Pacific coast have driven persistent cloud cover and scattered showers over Tokyo through September 8, limiting solar heating and capping daytime highs. Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models indicate maximum temperatures most likely between 28–30 °C under mostly cloudy, humid conditions with 50–70 % rain chances, consistent with the market's tight clustering around those outcomes. Elevated soil moisture from prior downpours adds evaporative cooling, while light southerly winds offer minimal mixing. New JMA guidance and updated model runs on September 7 will refine the precise peak, as small shifts in cloud timing or front position could tip the daily maximum by 1–2 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover and widespread thunderstorms forecast for Tokyo on September 7 are moderating daytime heating, with official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models pointing to a maximum near 26–28°C amid southerly flow and high humidity. Heavy rainfall and limited solar insolation suppress temperatures below early-September climatological norms, while evaporative cooling from prolonged precipitation further caps peaks. Trader consensus clusters around 27°C and 28°C because model runs show only modest differences in shower timing and intensity that could shift the daily high by 1–2°C, with newer guidance emphasizing continued overcast conditions rather than any rapid clearing that might allow brief warming.

**Persistent rain, heavy cloud cover, and northeasterly flow are keeping Tokyo's daytime temperatures suppressed on September 6, 2026, positioning 23°C and 24°C as the clear market leaders.** Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple models project a daily maximum of 24°C, with current observations showing readings near 22–23°C amid ongoing showers and thunderstorms. High humidity (often above 90%), low-level stratus, and moderate winds from the northeast limit solar heating and convective warming, preventing the warmer conditions typical for early September. 

These factors explain the strong trader consensus around the 23–24°C range (combined ~98% implied probability), while probabilities for 25°C or higher remain negligible given the entrenched wet pattern. Updated model runs and real-time surface observations continue to reinforce this cooler, unsettled regime through the afternoon and evening.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent heavy rain and thunderstorms expected across the Kanto region on September 7, driven by a northward-advancing Pacific front, represent the main factor capping trader-implied odds near 27–28°C. Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance lists a 28°C maximum under widespread cloud cover and precipitation probabilities exceeding 70 percent through the afternoon, limiting solar insolation and surface heating. Southerly flow and high humidity further moderate daytime peaks, consistent with multiple numerical models showing only modest warming despite seasonal norms near 29°C. The tight spread between 27°C and 28°C outcomes in the market reflects remaining uncertainty in the precise timing and intensity of heaviest rainfall, with final resolution dependent on afternoon observations from Tokyo stations.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts indicate cloudy skies with occasional scattered showers for Tokyo on September 8, limiting solar heating and supporting a maximum near 29°C, close to the early-September climatological average of 28.8°C. Persistent moisture from a stalled Pacific front, combined with southerly flow and high humidity, favors modest daytime warming while raising the chance of brief cooling from showers. Ensemble model guidance shows some spread in peak temperatures depending on exact cloud timing and rainfall intensity, creating the tight clustering around 28–30°C outcomes in trader pricing. Updated JMA briefings and next model runs will provide key resolution signals ahead of the date.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This aligns with the market-implied 86.5% probability for 23°C as the daily high, as moist, stable air and reduced solar insolation limit warming compared to typical early-September climatology. Recent model runs show minimal disagreement, with afternoon readings unlikely to reach 24°C thresholds amid ongoing precipitation. Traders are weighting these verified meteorological conditions heavily, with only modest implied odds for slight upward revisions if clearing occurs late in the day.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Heavy rainfall and persistent cloud cover from an approaching weather system are suppressing daytime heating in Tokyo on September 7, keeping the highest temperature in a narrow range centered on 27°C.** Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple models project a high near 26–28°C amid 90–100% precipitation probability, southerly winds of 10–20 km/h, and near-100% cloud cover that limits insolation. High humidity near 90% and dew points around 24–25°C further moderate peak readings by enhancing evaporative cooling and reducing the diurnal temperature range. With September climatological normals near 29°C, the expected widespread thunderstorms differentiate the tightly clustered market probabilities for 26–28°C outcomes, as small shifts in rain timing or wind direction could tip the daily maximum by 1–2°C. Updated model runs and JMA briefings tomorrow morning will provide the final data influencing resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Model consensus remains stable in recent runs, with limited spread due to predictable steering patterns and minimal instability. Traders price in small upside risk to 82-83°F (7%) if mixing is stronger than expected, while lower bins reflect the low chance of persistent cloudiness or a stronger marine influence. Official NWS updates and new model cycles over the next 24 hours will provide the next key data points for resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts for New York City on September 8 project a daytime maximum of 81–82°F under high pressure, light northwest winds, and mostly sunny to partly cloudy conditions that limit cloud cover and moisture. This setup favors moderate radiational heating consistent with early September climatology, where Central Park’s 1991–2020 average high is 79°F. Ensemble guidance and short-range models show little spread, keeping the highest probability centered on 82–83°F while assigning secondary weight to 80–81°F. No significant warm-air advection or subsidence strengthening is indicated in the latest runs, supporting the current market-implied odds with high confidence two days ahead of the event.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent heavy rain and cloud cover from a developing linear precipitation band are keeping Tokyo's maximum temperature locked near 23°C on September 6, 2026, driving the market's overwhelming 97% implied probability for that exact outcome.**

Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and multiple forecast models show sustained northeasterly flow, high humidity (90%+), and widespread precipitation that began intensifying during the day, suppressing solar heating and preventing the usual September afternoon rise. Real-time observations confirm temperatures hovering in the low 20s °C amid ongoing rain, consistent with the day's climatological suppression relative to the ~28–29°C seasonal average high. 

The dominant trader consensus reflects this strong, convergent data from authoritative sources, with only minimal probability assigned to a late-day spike that would push the high to 24°C or above. A realistic challenge would require an earlier-than-expected break in the clouds or significantly lighter rainfall allowing brief insolation, though current model consensus and ongoing precipitation make such a shift unlikely before the daily maximum is reached.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Persistent frontal moisture and scattered showers are the main factors capping Tokyo's September 8 maximum near 28–30 °C.** A stationary front off the Pacific coast has driven heavy rain across the Kanto region on September 7, with residual clouds, high humidity, and occasional showers expected to continue into Tuesday, reducing surface heating and limiting the daily peak. Japan Meteorological Agency guidance currently projects a high of 29 °C under mostly cloudy conditions with scattered showers, consistent with ensemble model consensus showing modest daytime insolation. This aligns with late-summer climatology (normal high ~28.8 °C) while the wet pattern suppresses the upper tail of the distribution. Traders are weighting outcomes around 28–30 °C most heavily because further model runs and JMA updates on steering flow and precipitation timing will determine whether breaks in cloud cover allow a brief push to 30 °C or keep readings closer to 28 °C.
